review.source: Actual written N1904 and original Berean publisher rows, reviewed against displayed BSB; distinct peer pending.

11:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς διατάσσων τοῖς δώδεκα μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ, μετέβη ἐκεῖθεν τοῦ διδάσκειν καὶ κηρύσσειν ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν αὐτῶν.
11:1.targetText: After Jesus had finished instructing His twelve disciples, He went on from there to teach and preach in their cities.

groups.note: Actual temporal ὅτε introduces the eventual sequence. English uses after with its past-perfect clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek narrative and-it-happened frame is implicit in the English temporal clause.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:2.sourceText: Ὁ δὲ Ἰωάνης ἀκούσας ἐν τῷ δεσμωτηρίῳ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Χριστοῦ, πέμψας διὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ
11:2.targetText: Meanwhile John heard in prison about the works of Christ, and he sent his disciples

groups.note: Exact publisher name is the same referent with a second nu. Retain actual N1904 Ἰωάνης.
Actual direct object works becomes a topic complement in English heard about.
Actual third-person sending participle supplies the English finite subject and verb.

unmappedSource.reason: English recasts sending through the disciples as sending them directly and omits the source preposition.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a conjunction between its two finite clauses. Actual hearing and sending are participial.

11:3.sourceText: εἶπεν αὐτῷ Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος, ἢ ἕτερον προσδοκῶμεν;
11:3.targetText: to ask Him, “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”

groups.note: Actual nominalizing article introduces the coming participle.
The actual present coming participle supplies this English future-in-the-past expression.

11:4.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάνει ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ βλέπετε·
11:4.targetText: Jesus replied, “Go back and report to John what you hear and see:

groups.note: Actual answering participle and said verb supply one English reply predicate.

studyHeads.note: Actual answering participle contributes the reply sense.

groups.note: Actual dative Ἰωάνει supplies the recipient. The publisher writes Ἰωάννῃ.

unmappedSource.reason: The initial coordinator and the reply’s dative recipients are not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: The translation coordinates a travel command with reporting. Actual travelling is participial.

11:5.sourceText: τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν καὶ χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν, λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν, καὶ νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται καὶ πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται·
11:5.targetText: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.

unmappedSource.reason: The English list punctuation leaves these three printed conjunctions implicit.

11:6.sourceText: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί.
11:6.targetText: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me.”

groups.note: Actual relative and conditional particle form the indefinite construction.
Actual stumbling passive predicate supplies the recast auxiliary and predicate under its separate negative.

unmappedSource.reason: English opens the blessing after the preceding list without a separate conjunction.

11:7.sourceText: Τούτων δὲ πορευομένων ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγειν τοῖς ὄχλοις περὶ Ἰωάνου Τί ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι; κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον;
11:7.targetText: As John’s disciples were leaving, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?

groups.note: English names the people referred to by the actual demonstrative these. No new literal John or disciple token is assigned here.
Actual genitive-absolute leaving participle supplies the temporal clause and its lexical verb.
Actual dative crowd noun supplies the recipient relation.
Actual Ἰωάνου has a different spelling from the publisher Ἰωάννου. This is the actual later personal name, distinct from the earlier demonstrative.

unmappedSource.reason: English opens the temporal clause without a separate continuation connective.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:8.sourceText: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἠμφιεσμένον; ἰδοὺ οἱ τὰ μαλακὰ φοροῦντες ἐν τοῖς οἴκοις τῶν βασιλέων.
11:8.targetText: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear fine clothing are found in kings’ palaces.

groups.note: Actual nominalizing article marks the people characterized by wearing.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: The publisher Greek includes εἰσίν here. Actual N1904 lacks that copula, and no finding verb is printed.

11:9.sourceText: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε; προφήτην ἰδεῖν; ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου.
11:9.targetText: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.

11:10.sourceText: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου.
11:10.targetText: This is the one about whom it is written:  ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’

groups.note: Actual before preposition supplies the English directional relation.
Actual possessive of the omitted face noun corresponds to the first explicit English You.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual face in before your face is implicit in the English ahead-of expression.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English spells out the identity introduced by this and the actual copula.

11:11.sourceText: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ ἐγήγερται ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν μείζων Ἰωάνου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ· ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.
11:11.targetText: Truly I tell you, among those born of women there has risen no one greater than John the Baptist. Yet even the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

groups.note: Actual genitive John supplies the first standard of comparison. The actual single nu remains.

unmappedTarget.reason: English emphasizes the comparison without a distinct local source particle.

11:12.sourceText: ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν ἡμερῶν Ἰωάνου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ ἕως ἄρτι ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν βιάζεται, καὶ βιασταὶ ἁρπάζουσιν αὐτήν.
11:12.targetText: From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven has been subject to violence, and the violent lay claim to it.

groups.note: Actual genitive John supplies the first relation of John, distinct from of heaven.

unmappedSource.reason: The continuation connective is implicit at the start of the English sentence.

11:13.sourceText: πάντες γὰρ οἱ προφῆται καὶ ὁ νόμος ἕως Ἰωάνου ἐπροφήτευσαν·
11:13.targetText: For all the Prophets and the Law prophesied until John.

groups.note: Actual printed Ἰωάνου is the same named person as exact publisher Ἰωάννου.

11:14.sourceText: καὶ εἰ θέλετε δέξασθαι, αὐτός ἐστιν Ἡλείας ὁ μέλλων ἔρχεσθαι.
11:14.targetText: And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come.

groups.note: Actual Ἡλείας has a different spelling from publisher Ἠλίας. The corresponding named person remains exact.
Actual nominalizing article introduces the about-to participle.
Actual present about-to participle supplies the English prospective frame under English past wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of acceptance. The actual infinitive has none explicitly printed.

11:15.targetText: He who has ears, let him hear.

11:16.sourceText: Τίνι δὲ ὁμοιώσω τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην; ὁμοία ἐστὶν παιδίοις καθημένοις ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ἃ προσφωνοῦντα τοῖς ἑτέροις
11:16.targetText: To what can I compare this generation? They are like children sitting in the marketplaces and calling out to others:

groups.note: Actual singular copula is rendered with English plural agreement with the contextual group.

unmappedSource.reason: The English question opens without the actual continuation connective.
Actual relative subject is implicit in the reformulated coordinated description.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a plural anaphor for this generation. There is no written subject pronoun in the comparison.
English coordinates sitting and calling in place of the actual relative clause.

11:17.sourceText: λέγουσιν Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε· ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκόψασθε·
11:17.targetText: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn.’

groups.note: Actual first dancing predicate supplies the English subject, auxiliary and verb.
Actual second mourning predicate supplies the English subject, auxiliary and verb.

unmappedSource.reason: English opens the quotation without an overt local saying predicate.

11:18.sourceText: ἦλθεν γὰρ Ἰωάνης μήτε ἐσθίων μήτε πίνων, καὶ λέγουσιν Δαιμόνιον ἔχει.
11:18.targetText: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon!’

groups.note: Official Berean source prints Ἰωάννης; the actual N1904 Ἰωάνης remains exact.

11:19.sourceText: ἦλθεν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγουσιν Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, τελωνῶν φίλος καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν. καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῆς.
11:19.targetText: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is vindicated by her actions.”

groups.note: Actual attention marker, traditionally behold, supplies the English imperative phrase.
Actual man and glutton describe one speaker-introduced figure.

studyHeads.note: Actual glutton word supplies the lexical head.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English specifies the subject of the attention marker with an added demonstrative.

11:20.sourceText: Τότε ἤρξατο ὀνειδίζειν τὰς πόλεις ἐν αἷς ἐγένοντο αἱ πλεῖσται δυνάμεις αὐτοῦ, ὅτι οὐ μετενόησαν·
11:20.targetText: Then Jesus began to denounce the cities in which most of His miracles had been performed, because they did not repent.

groups.note: Actual third-plural repentance supplies the subject, auxiliary and verb under the separate negator.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds the contextual name of the one beginning to denounce. No local name is printed.

11:21.sourceText: Οὐαί σοι, Χοραζείν· οὐαί σοι, Βηθσαϊδάν· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἐγένοντο αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν ὑμῖν, πάλαι ἂν ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ μετενόησαν.
11:21.targetText: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

groups.note: The precise publisher proper name confirms the exact actual Χοραζείν occurrence.
The precise publisher name confirms actual Βηθσαϊδάν, including its distinct final nu.
The actual counterfactual particle and repenting predicate jointly supply the English modal form.

studyHeads.note: Actual modal particle gives the counterfactual relation.
Actual aorist repenting supplies the lexical head.

11:22.sourceText: πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ ὑμῖν.
11:22.targetText: But I tell you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.

11:23.sourceText: καὶ σύ, Καφαρναούμ, μὴ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ; ἕως Ἅιδου καταβήσῃ· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Σοδόμοις ἐγενήθησαν αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν σοί, ἔμεινεν ἂν μέχρι τῆς σήμερον.
11:23.targetText: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Sodom, it would have remained to this day.

groups.note: Actual negative question particle anticipates a negative answer. English states that answer before the following contrast.
Actual Ἅιδου corresponds to the publisher’s Hades reference. The source version remains unchanged.
Actual descending predicate is recast as a passive English phrase.
Actual counterfactual particle and remaining predicate supply the English modal form.

studyHeads.note: Actual modal particle marks the counterfactual conclusion.
The actual remaining verb supplies the lexical head.

groups.note: Actual today adverb supplies the English time phrase, without treating the article as a demonstrative.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:24.sourceText: πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι γῇ Σοδόμων ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ σοί.
11:24.targetText: But I tell you that it will be more bearable for Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.”

groups.note: Actual dative land-of-Sodom construction supplies the first dative relation, without expressing land independently.

11:25.sourceText: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἐξομολογοῦμαί σοι, Πάτερ, Κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἔκρυψας ταῦτα ἀπὸ σοφῶν καὶ συνετῶν, καὶ ἀπεκάλυψας αὐτὰ νηπίοις·
11:25.targetText: At that time Jesus declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.

groups.note: Actual answering and saying are recast as one finite declaration.

studyHeads.note: Actual saying supplies the main speech predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:26.sourceText: ναί, ὁ Πατήρ, ὅτι οὕτως εὐδοκία ἐγένετο ἔμπροσθέν σου.
11:26.targetText: Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.

groups.note: Actual before/in-the-presence preposition supplies the split English circumstantial phrase.
Actual definite possessor of the addressee supplies Your.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:27.sourceText: Πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατρός μου, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπιγινώσκει τὸν Υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ Πατήρ, οὐδὲ τὸν Πατέρα τις ἐπιγινώσκει εἰ μὴ ὁ Υἱὸς καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ Υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι.
11:27.targetText: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.

groups.note: Actual if not supplies the first exception.
Actual second negative coordinator supplies the additive continuation and its separate negative.
Actual indefinite anyone supplies the second subject under the separate negator.
Actual second if not supplies the separate exception.
Actual relative with its modal particle supplies the English indefinite group.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual continuation connective is implicit at the English sentence break.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes the object of revealing explicit. The local Greek infinitive has no separately written object.

11:28.sourceText: Δεῦτε πρός με πάντες οἱ κοπιῶντες καὶ πεφορτισμένοι, κἀγὼ ἀναπαύσω ὑμᾶς.
11:28.targetText: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.

groups.note: Actual causative resting predicate supplies both English verbal pieces.
Actual accusative recipients supply the second You-related word in the English verse, distinct from the nominalizing address.

11:29.sourceText: ἄρατε τὸν ζυγόν μου ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς καὶ μάθετε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι πραΰς εἰμι καὶ ταπεινὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ, καὶ εὑρήσετε ἀνάπαυσιν ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν·
11:29.targetText: Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.

groups.note: Actual dative heart supplies the scope expressed by in.
Actual dative souls supplies the beneficiary expressed by the later for.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:30.sourceText: ὁ γὰρ ζυγός μου χρηστὸς καὶ τὸ φορτίον μου ἐλαφρόν ἐστιν.
11:30.targetText: For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.”

groups.note: The one actual copula supplies both coordinated nominal predicates. English repeats it.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
